title: Writing the Nest opening and 'Walk, Jenny, Walk' with Henry Creamer
summary: Wooding and lyricist Henry Creamer write the show opening in twenty minutes and turn his song into 'Walk, Jenny, Walk', placed by a song plugger.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: "Tweet-tweet, twat-twat." That was the first of the scat singers. The same as -- this was a new period coming in altogether and they came in with us at the Nest. Now when I went to the Nest, it was the first time I had had some experience in composing, I guess. But all of a sudden that's come to me and I had my song, "Walk, Jenny, Walk". A fellow come in, Johnny Carey come home and said, "I want you to meet one of our old songwriters, Henry Creamer." Henry Creamer had written "Way Down South in New Orleans", "Whoa, Tilly, Whoa", and some other things along with Turner Layton. See this was a -- Turner Layton and Henry Creamer had broken up now. Layton was going with -- to become Layton and Johnson, and so Henry Creamer was free-lancing. So Johnny said, Johnny Carey said, "This man is going to write the words to our beginning, the introduction of our show." I said, "My opening is going to be twenty minutes", he said, "can you supply him with the music, Sam?" I said, "Certainly". So he sat down there beside the piano and I said, "Well, Henry, read the words off." And he read some things like the birds in their nest and then asked some things like -- well I'll put a -- so I started writing the music and inside twenty minutes, we had the opening.
What is that song like. Do you remember the song, "Walk, Jenny, Walk".
No, it was like an opening, it wasn't exactly a song.
Uh hunh. Do you remember how it goes?
(plays piano and sings) -- We're the boys of the Nest, we're the people of the Nest and we're here to entertain you -- and all that. But, between sets, in twenty minutes time, we had the thing.
Uh hunh. Tell me about -- oh, you --

So I was gonna say, so Henry, he and I liked -- were so fluent at it, so he said, "Kid, you got any songs?" "Yeah, I got one particular one, it's 'Walk, Johnny, Walk'. And I say, "Well, I think it's going to be good." And so tomorrow afternoon we made an appointment, and we met and he said, "That sounds good.", but he said, "But nobody wants to hear no man walk." He said, "Look, let's fix this and use the same words and all that, but we'll make it into a woman, and say 'Walk, Jenny, Walk', because who's going to watch a man walking down the street." Well, he made sense, so we jumped into it, and I said, "What are we going to do with it?" And he said, "Well, I've got a friend of mine that's a song plugger, and he'll plug this song and make something." And the next
day, when we had finished and had it all straightened out and it was "Walk, Jenny, Walk", instead of "Walk, Johnny, Walk", why we met Bob Schafer, and that's how that got started.
So you see, I was building something then I didn't realize I was building.
